question: Is 'deleting the metal repairs the embedding' a property of our generated complexes, or of RDKit's embedder applied to metal complexes in general?

cohort_provenance.real: /home/hugo/codes/mol-metal/.data/molmetal/tmQM/tmqm_parsed.csv -- REAL tmQM SMILES with their metal identity. NOT real_tmqm_reference.csv, which the BLK-C-L4 audit showed is 636/636 decoder output with bracket-atom notation and would measure our bond head against itself.

VERDICT.verdict: LOCALISATION DOES NOT SURVIVE the control: RDKit repairs real tmQM metal complexes at nearly the same rate as it repairs the generated ones, so '11 of 12 embed once the metal is deleted' is a base rate of the embedder, not evidence about our bond head. next_actions[0] and the L5 localisation must be re-scoped before any fix is designed.

what_this_does_not_settle: n is still small on the generated side (12 failures). This establishes whether the effect is worth pursuing, not its size.
Embeddability is a proxy. It says nothing about whether the complex is a plausible anticancer agent -- the ligand set and geometry still have to be judged separately.
